reasonToGo: The river's last reach, and the only walked ground on Reedstrand that carries any river at all — 0.9 per cent of it here, 0.5 on one reported lobe, and nothing in the other six regions. The delta's single village stands on the levee above it. Below the levee the mangrove is cut for stakes, and outside the levee the reef and the drowned valley put enough on the shore to keep a salvage crew working between spates.

hazards.name: Last year's channel
hazards.description: The braid re-cuts itself every spate and the bar at the mouth moves with it. A loaded boat that takes the channel it took last season goes on the bar broadside to whatever swell is running, and the crews sound the mouth again after every flood for exactly this reason.

hazards.name: The oxbow fever
hazards.description: The cut-off bends behind the levee hold water the river has abandoned and the tide still reaches twice a month. It is neither fresh nor salt and it does not move. A crew that waters above the ford instead of at it is a crew short by the third week.

resources.name: Platform salvage
resources.description: Worked off the cut platform and the drowned valley inside the reef, which between them take a hull and then lay out what is left of it within a tide. It is picked over after every gale rather than dug for, and what is not lifted before the next spate is moved somewhere nobody has looked.

resources.name: Mangrove stakes
resources.description: Cut at the mouth from one of only three mangrove flats drawn anywhere in the world, and the only wood standing on this ground. It goes to stakes, hurdle and boat frame; nothing growing here is straight enough or long enough to saw into a plank.

landmarks.name: Quillfall Reach
landmarks.description: The last straight water above the braid, deep enough on a flood to bring a laden boat right up to the levee and shallow enough on the ebb to leave it there. The village on the bank above it is the only settlement drawn anywhere on Reedstrand.

landmarks.name: Stack below Brightlobe
landmarks.description: The seaward end of the reach, where the cut platform runs out under the reef and the drowned valley turns in behind it. Nothing stands off this shore; the mark is the line of broken water over the platform edge, which is visible from the levee and from nowhere further inland.
